title: Corinthians Aim to Climb Brasileirão Table Against Chapecoense
seoTitle: Corinthians Seek Table Climb Against Chapecoense
subtitle: A win could lift the Timão from 11th to 10th place and close the gap to the G5
excerpt: With 32 points in 11th place, Corinthians face Chapecoense this round. A win could lift the club to 10th, bringing them closer to the top group.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Corinthians take the field tonight against Chapecoense needing points to improve their position in the Campeonato Brasileiro standings. The match, valid for the 26th round, could change the Timão's position and narrow the gap to the G5.

Current position and points

After 25 rounds, the team led by Fernando Diniz sits in 11th place with 32 points and an overall success rate of 42 %. In the general standings, the club is eight points behind the group that secures a spot in the 2027 pre-Libertadores and seven points clear of the relegation zone.

What a win against Chapecoense could change

A victory would take Corinthians to 35 points, surpassing São Paulo, who had already played, and taking tenth place. The club would be tied on points with ninth-placed Red Bull Bragantino, but ahead on number of wins (ten against nine). In addition, the gap to Bahia, the current leader of the G5, would drop to eight points.

Consequences of a draw or defeat

If the match ends in a draw, the Timão will remain in 11th place, potentially dropping to 12th if Botafogo beats Palmeiras. A loss would keep the tally at 32 points and open the possibility of dropping to 14th place if Botafogo, Santos, and Vitória win their matches this round, bringing the club closer to the 25 points of Vasco da Gama, who currently open the relegation zone.

Recent performance in the second half of the season

In the second half of the season, Corinthians have played six matches, claiming only one win – over Red Bull Bragantino – and recording two draws (against Bahia and Athletico-PR). The Alvinegro's success rate in this period is 28 %, ranking ahead of only Botafogo (27 %), Internacional (22 %), and Vitória (17 %). Atlético-MG leads this stretch with 73 %.

Campaign context and expectations

Since 2018, the club has found knockout competitions to be its only chance to compete for silverware, while in the Brasileirão it has never returned to the top three and has finished in the bottom ten in four editions. The streak of three consecutive defeats – against Cruzeiro, Coritiba, and Santos – has ramped up the pressure to get back to winning ways and regain momentum in the push for the upper part of the table.

With information from UOL, Meu Timão.
